text:
Ashley: heads-up — vendor 'AureliaAI' sent over a new LLM package (weights + tokenizer) that we want to onboard to private deployment. need a short checklist for artifact acquisition, provenance checks, and registry/storage steps. TL;DR: weights ~12GB, tokenizer files, model card, license.

Ravi: +1. quick checklist to start: 1) get signed vendor manifest, 2) checksum weights/tokenizer, 3) ingest to content-addressable bucket, 4) attach metadata (model_id/version/license/sha256/source_uri), 5) run lightweight download+load smoke test on a dedicated sandbox GPU, 6) scan for secrets and PII.

Jordan: FYI our registry expects these metadata fields: model_name, model_version, source_uri, source_type, license, sha256, file_sizes, tokenizer_hash, provenance_url, owner, allowed_environments, tags. We'll want an entry like:
```json
{
  "model_name": "aurelia-mini-v1",
  "model_version": "2026-03-01",
  "source_uri": "s3://redwood-models/aurelia/aurelia-mini-v1/weights-20260301.bin",
  "sha256": "<calc_here>",
  "tokenizer": "s3://redwood-models/aurelia/aurelia-mini-v1/tokenizer.json",
  "license": "custom-noncommercial-v1",
  "provenance": "https://vendor.example.com/manifests/aurelia-mini-v1",
  "tags": ["llama-derivative","candidate","needs-quant-test"]
}
```

Ravi: use content-addressable keys to dedupe: compute sha256 on the raw bytes and store at s3://redwood-cas/<sha256>.weights. Example commands:
```
sha256sum weights.bin
aws s3 cp weights.bin s3://redwood-cas/$(sha256sum weights.bin | awk '{print $1}').weights --acl bucket-owner-full-control
aws s3 cp tokenizer.json s3://redwood-cas/$(sha256sum tokenizer.json | awk '{print $1}').tokenizer --acl bucket-owner-full-control
```

Sam: infra notes — use a short-lived presigned URL for vendor upload, then we copy into our buckets under an ingest account that has restricted KMS key for at-rest encryption. Also add S3 object metadata: x-amz-meta-source=vendor-aurelia, x-amz-meta-manifest-uri=..., x-amz-meta-license=... so quick audit queries work.

Katie: security checklist: 1) confirm vendor identity + contract clause for model provenance, 2) validate manifest signature (PGP or sigstore ideally), 3) run weight scanner (basic heuristics + entropy checks) for appended secrets or steganography, 4) run tokenizer + small decode tests to detect embedded PII, 5) require privacy/DR plan if training data provenance is partial. If vendor cannot sign, escalate to legal/sales.

Jordan: tokenizer hashes matter — different tokenizers with same weights can change behavior. compute tokenizer_hash = sha256(tokenizer.json) and store separate artifact. For reproducibility, snapshot exact tokenizer lib version (e.g., tokenizers==0.15.3) and python runtime.

Ashley: good point. We'll include runtime snapshot in metadata. Example metadata we want attached to registry entry (flat key-values):
```
meta.model_id = aurelia-mini-v1
meta.model_version = 2026-03-01
meta.sha256 = <sha256-of-weights>
meta.tokenizer_hash = <sha256-of-tokenizer>
meta.tokenizer_lib = tokenizers==0.15.3
meta.runtime = python==3.10,torch==2.2
meta.license = custom-noncommercial-v1
meta.provenance_url = https://vendor.example.com/manifests/aurelia-mini-v1
meta.vendor_signature = <sigfile-url-or-blank>
```

Ravi: for quantization experiments: tag the registry entry with 'quant-candidate' and push a pointer to the raw weights in a quarantine bucket accessible only to eng-ml and quant infra. We'll produce a 4-bit quantized variant and store as s3://redwood-variants/<sha256>-q4. Keep original immutable.

Sam: we should also create an ephemeral deployment with resource limits for the smoke test: 1 request/min, sequence len 256, run eval harness (basic perplexity + a small prompt set) and log outputs to the model-evals bucket. If outputs differ significantly from vendor sample, hold.

Katie: add this to the security gating: run the eval harness on private data-free prompt set + vendor sample. If quality regression > threshold (we use delta-EM or ROUGE-like metric depending on task) then we mark as 'needs-investigation'.

Jordan: storage lifecycle: store original weights in cold tier after 90 days unless flagged critical. But the registry entry should always keep manifest + checksum + provenance_url persisted. Also keep a small 'reference' quantized build for quick inference.

Ashley: procedural asks: who will 1) request vendor signed manifest, 2) compute checksums + upload to CAS, 3) create registry entry, 4) run smoke tests? I can do 1 & 3 if others can help with 2 and 4.

Ravi: I can take 2 (checksum + CAS upload) — I'll need vendor presigned upload or we pull from vendor URL. Also need KMS key id.

Sam: I can handle 4 (smoke test + ephemeral deployment). I'll add the eval job to CI-runner sandbox and post logs.

Katie: I'll review the manifest signature and run the weight/tokenizer scanners. If any issues, I'll flag and route to legal/security.

ci-bot: created checklist ticket #ML-1204 with tasks: vendor-manifest, compute-sha, cas-ingest, registry-entry, smoke-test, security-scan. Assigned: Ashley(R), Ravi(A), Sam(A), Katie(R). Link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/ML-1204

Ashley: perfect. one more question — how do we capture provenance lineage if vendor later issues a patched version? Do we version by sha and link to prior?

Jordan: yes, registry model_version must be immutable and canonicalized to the sha. If patched, new entry with new model_version and 'replaces' pointer to prior sha. Keep provenance_url per-version.

Ravi: operational note: add two automated checks on registry ingestion: 1) validate sha matches object in CAS, 2) ensure metadata keys present (license, provenance_url, tokenizer_hash). If any fail, ingestion api returns 422.

Ashley: thanks all — I'll start the vendor outreach for the signed manifest and post updates here. Ravi/Sam/Katie follow up in ticket ML-1204. :thumbsup:
